sets.title: Authorization decision in three distinct control-flow forms
sets.description: The same resource-authorization decision in three policy classes, each written in a genuinely different control-flow form: carrier A uses early-return guard clauses (pristine), carrier B uses a combined precondition guard plus a match(true) dispatch, carrier C uses nested conditionals with a single result variable. All three are hand-written and proven behaviorally identical. No two carriers share a token run long enough for a token/line tool to pair them, so only AST-canonicalizing and semantic detectors are expected to recover the cluster.
sets.notes: Guard-clause (A), match-dispatch (B) and nested-conditional (C) forms are proven behaviorally identical by gen/seeds/access_guard/equivalence_test.php over the full input matrix. The three bodies are pairwise token-distinct (no member pair shares a >=40 normalized Type-2 token run), so a token detector finds no pair at all — recovering the full three-member cluster requires seeing through the control-flow rewrite, consistent with token_based=false. min_members_for_credit is the default 2.
